statement: The command is written NLGEOM,Key and is documented to 'Include large-deflection effects in a static or full transient analysis.'
NLGEOM is categorized under the SOLUTION solution area as 'Nonlinear Options'.
The Key argument is described as the 'Large-deflection key'.
NLGEOM,OFF 'Ignores large-deflection effects (that is, a small-deflection analysis is specified)' and this option is the default.
NLGEOM,ON 'Includes large-deflection (large rotation) effects or large strain effects, according to the element type.'
The command default is that 'Large-deflection effects are ignored'.
Large-deflection effects are categorized as either large deflection (or large rotation) or large strain, depending on the element type.
When large deflection effects are included (NLGEOM,ON), stress stiffening effects are also included automatically.
If used during the solution (/SOLU), the NLGEOM command is valid only within the first load step.
In a large-deflection analysis, pressure loads behave differently than other load types.
The gyroscopic matrix (that occurs due to rotational angular velocity) does not support large-deflection effects; its formulation supports small deflection only.
When large-deflection effects are included in a substructure or CMS transient analysis use pass, the OUTRES command ignores DSUBres = ALL.
The NLGEOM command is also valid in the PREP7 preprocessing phase.
NLGEOM is accessible from the GUI via Main Menu>Preprocessor>Loads>Analysis Type>Analysis Options.
NLGEOM is accessible from the GUI via Main Menu>Solution>Analysis Type>Analysis Options and Solution>Sol'n Controls>Basic.

NLGEOM,ON is the APDL switch that enables large-deflection/large-strain (nonlinear geometry) behavior, recomputing element stiffness from the deformed configuration including geometric stiffness effects (SSAT/KG).
NLGEOM,ON is the alias form NLGEOM,1 in APDL and the two are used interchangeably.
NLGEOM,ON is required wherever rotations, slenderness effects, buckling margins or large strain matter.

Verified spellings of the command are NLGEOM,ON, nlgeom,on and alias NLGEOM,1, seen across sample_usr.dat, threaded_connection.dat, extrusion.dat, wirecrimp.dat, springcoil.dat, stent.dat, buckling.dat, cylinderflat.dat, Hot_Rolling_Model.dat and SequentialEmbankmentCase1/Case2.dat.
NLGEOM,ON is turned on in the verified tutorials for every large-deformation case under static, transient, soil (ANTYPE,SOIL) and forming analyses, alongside large-strain material models and contact.
NLGEOM is used with the buckling example (td-21) for buckling and post-buckling of a ring-stiffened cylinder, with nlgeom,on annotated 'Large deflection is activated'.
NLGEOM,ON is used with the hot-rolling example (td-27) for 3D rezoning, annotated 'Turn on nonlinear geometry effects'.
NLGEOM,ON is used with the sequential embankment (soil) example (td-52) under ANTYPE,SOIL/geostatic, annotated 'LARGE DEFORMATION TURNED ON'.
The buckling Load-control example script issues NLGEOM,1 within the /SOL (SOLUTION) phase before NSUBST and AUTOTS.
A Technology Showcase example script issues 'NLGEOM, ON   ! Activate large deflection' in the SOLUTION phase after NROPT,UNSYM for a static solve.
The Basic Analysis Guide shows NLGEOM,ON in an example structural transient input listing (ANTYPE,TRANS; TRNOPT,FULL; NLGEOM,ON).
The Basic Analysis Guide notes that in a large-deformation analysis (NLGEOM,ON) the element coordinate system is first rotated by the computed rotations.
The Basic Analysis Guide notes that when large rotations (NLGEOM,ON) are used, a static analysis with inertia relief is not exactly valid.
The Advanced Analysis Guide requires 'Static analysis with geometric nonlinearity (NLGEOM,ON)' for the 2D-to-3D analysis support.
For element birth and death, unless large-deformation effects are activated (NLGEOM,ON), some element types are reactivated in their originally specified geometric configuration.
For a structural analysis employing element birth and death, the guide instructs to activate large-deflection effects (NLGEOM,ON) in the first load step.
The Advanced Analysis Guide sample first-load-step input includes 'NLGEOM,ON  ! Turns large-deflection effects on' followed by NROPT,FULL.
A transient analysis example in the Advanced Analysis Guide uses geometric nonlinearity activated via NLGEOM,ON.
